findingMessages.naming.pick-lightroom-catalog-typed-pick: `pick_lightroom_catalog` is typed `Option<PickFolder>` (alias doc: 'A folder chooser') but the only implementation calls `.pick_file()` with a `.lrcat` filter and returns a file path. The alias is used for a file picker, so a new host (web/Linux/test) reading the type will implement a folder dialog and hand back a directory that the importer then rejects, and `PickFolder` no longer means 'folder'.
findingMessages.naming.crop-and-mask-overlay-name-collis: In panels/detail.rs `fn crop_overlay` draws the crop box and its handles, while `app.ui.crop_overlay` (state.rs:560) is the guide style (thirds/grid/spiral) and `super::crop_overlay::paths` (line 1398, inside that very function) is a third `crop_overlay` module; `fn mask_overlay` draws outlines/pins/brush while `ui.mask_overlay` (state.rs:550) toggles the rendered overlay of the mask (its own doc says the mask itself shows as `view_overlay`). The same word names four different things in one file, so a reader or grep for 'crop_overlay'/'mask_overlay' lands on the wrong concept and an edit to the toggle gets applied to the drawing function.
findingMessages.naming.ui-commands-fn-vs-const: `menus::ui_commands()` iterates LANGUAGE_COMMANDS then UI_COMMANDS, so the function named `ui_commands` returns a superset of the constant `UI_COMMANDS`. Callers that need every UI command must use the function while anyone grepping or reading `UI_COMMANDS` (xtask/src/parity.rs:4 cites 'a UI command from `UI_COMMANDS`') silently misses the language commands.
findingMessages.naming.left-panel-folder-polysemy: 'folder' means three things in left.rs: `folder_menu(.., a: &Album)` is the context menu of an album folder, `folder_menu_for_library(.., n: &FolderNode)` (with sibling `row_menu`) is the library Folders row menu, and `folder_tree` is a Local on-disk folder row while `folder_rows`/`folder_row` draw the library Folders section (and `Caches::folder_tree` in lib.rs:1587 is the library tree, not the Local one). Separately `folder_label(path)` returns a display name while `folder_label_menu` is the colour-label submenu. A change to 'folder_tree' or 'folder_menu' is easy to apply to the wrong sidebar section.
